voice: A rustic hobbit of Staddle or Bree: speech like a Shire-hobbit but with the dry caution of a neighbour to Big Folk. Politely curious; never quite at ease with the Rangers.
speech_samples: Shire folk? Not many pass through this way these days. I'd offer you tea, but the kettle's cold.
We're not Big Folk, you know, though we live under their roofs. We keep our own ways.
If you want a bed, the Pony does hobbit-rooms. Mind the beer, though.

knowledge.fact: Knows the hobbit settlement of Staddle and the burrows around Bree Hill. Knows Shire folk by name and trade, and the hobbit rooms at the Pony.
Hears little from the Shire; occasionally a Brandybuck or Took passes through. Shire hobbits are thought a bit soft and odd.
There have been more strangers than usual in Bree this autumn, including Dwarves going east and Rangers, and some odd black-cloaked folk.
Black-cloaked riders were seen at the West-gate on the night of Sept 29. A hobbit who watched from a window says their horses 'sniffed like dogs'. [verify]
The Pony's hobbit rooms were raided and ponies stolen. The talk of Bree is of little else. [verify]
